title: Bi-temporal Image-driven Acute Stroke Evolution Analysis
description:
Code for the IEEE BHI 2026 paper “Bi-temporal Image-driven Acute Stroke Evolution Analysis”.

Admission CT perfusion (CTP, T1) is registered to follow-up diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI, T2), and the two label sets are intersected into six outcome-aware region-of-interest classes. Each class pairs what the tissue looked like on admission with the fate it went on to have:

  • pen_brain — penumbra, salvaged
  • pen_fi — penumbra, progressed to infarct
  • core_brain — core, salvaged
  • core_fi — core, remained infarcted
  • clb_brain — contralateral healthy brain
  • nhb_fi — non-hypoperfused brain, later infarcted

Admission tissue is then described with four feature families: first-order statistics (FE1), GLCM radiomics (FE2), mJ-Net embeddings (FE3) and nnU-Net embeddings (FE4). Four region-pair comparisons are run at patient level, using a cosine separation index Δ̃cos for the CNN families, and Mann–Whitney U with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR and Cliff’s delta for the handcrafted ones.

Key findings. On the Stavanger University Hospital cohort (n = 109), salvaged and infarcted penumbra separate consistently (Δ̃cos = 0.146, p < 0.05), core tissue barely separates by subsequent fate (Δ̃cos = 0.031), and the largest separation is between initially non-hypoperfused tissue that later infarcted and healthy contralateral brain (Δ̃cos = 0.460). The same pattern holds on ISLES’24 (n = 149), supporting consistency across cohorts.

Contents. Preprocessing and registration through to the six ROI classes; the four feature extractors; and the analysis that reproduces the paper’s result tables. A synthetic cohort is included so the analysis stage runs end to end without patient data. Neither cohort is distributed here: the hospital cohort is not public, and ISLES’24 must be obtained from its organisers.
